messages.subject: choice perseveration in bandit4arm models
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

We would like to add a choice perseveration factor in the bandit4arm models, to see whether it improves the fit of the models.
To do this, I tried to calculate the lag-1 autocorrelation of the choice history, and then multiply it to a free parameter ("cons"), which in turn is added to the softmax of the value and noise. It is not working (please see script attached). Could anyone help me with this?

Thanks very much,

Flavia

messages.subject: Re: choice perseveration in bandit4arm models
messages.body_plain:
Hi Flavia,

As I checked your code attached, it seems the file has two problems. First, you didn't define "g" before Line 91. Adding a line with "real g;" near Line 80 will resolve the error. Second, you used the function "acf" in Line 91, but it works only on R but not on Stan. If you want to calculate the autocorrelation between choices on Stan, it would be better to define a custom function on Stan (see more on this link <https://mc-stan.org/docs/2_18/stan-users-guide/basic-functions-section.html>).

FYI, the latest version of RStudio <https://rstudio.com/> supports the Stan language and provides convenient features. I highly recommend you to check it out and try it by yourself.

Best,
Jaeyeong

messages.subject: Re: Priors for choiceRT_ddm
messages.body_plain:
Hi Adam,

Thanks for your interest and for the question!

So, the Phi_approx() function is an approximation to the inverse of the standard cumulative normal distribution. That said, because the mu_p is centered at 0 before going through the transformation, after the transformation the prior is actually centered at .5 like you suggest. We use this parameterization to ensure that parameters fall in (0,1).

Let me know if that's clear!

Best,
Nate

Sent by mobile phone

From: hbayesd...@googlegroups.com <hbayesd...@googlegroups.com> on behalf of Adam Bear <adam...@gmail.com>
Sent: Thursday, January 9, 2020 6:47:15 PM
To: hbayesdm-users <hbayesd...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: Priors for choiceRT_ddm

Hello,

I noticed in the choiceRT_ddm.stan code, the priors for the starting-point bias term of the DDM (beta) seem to be centered at 0; i.e.,

beta[i] = Phi_approx(mu_pr[2] + sigma[2] * beta_pr[I]).

Given that beta ranges between 0 and 1, and .5 is the midpoint indicating no bias (if I'm understanding the model properly), wouldn't it make sense to add .5 to the line above? With sufficient data, I'm sure this won't make a big difference for parameter estimates, but just thought this might be a bug worth fixing.

Best,
Adam
